nabers.name: Malik Nabers
nabers.currentStatus: Rehabbing torn ACL + meniscus. Second cleanup surgery (scar tissue removal) performed ~May 2026. Week 1 availability uncertain — HC John Harbaugh says recovery is "not simple." Target is training camp but no guarantee.

injuries.title: ACL + Meniscus Tear — Right Knee (Week 4, Sept 28, 2025)
injuries.detail: Tore ACL and meniscus while running a deep route vs. the Los Angeles Chargers. Stepped awkwardly with right leg before jumping for a Jaxson Dart pass. Carted off the field, placed on IR. Surgery performed ~late October 2025 (delayed one month post-injury). A second arthroscopic procedure was performed in May 2026 to remove scar tissue causing knee stiffness — a common complication after combined ACL/meniscus repairs (arthrofibrosis). HC Harbaugh stated the goal is Week 1 readiness but noted recovery is "not a simple" process. Research context: NFL WRs return to play after ACL reconstruction at a 60–69% rate, with an average return timeline of 10.9–13.6 months. Among WRs who do return, studies show significantly decreased targets, receptions, receiving yards, and TDs compared to pre-injury production and matched controls. Career length post-ACLR is shortened by an average of 1.9 seasons. Combined ACL + meniscus injuries carry added complexity and longer recovery timelines. Subsequent ACL injury risk (either knee) is approximately 25% within the first 2-3 years post-reconstruction.
injuries.source: CBS Sports, Newsweek, Bleacher Report, SIC Score — Orthopedic research: Arthroscopy, Sports Medicine and Rehabilitation (2021); OJSM (2021)

injuries.title: Concussion (Week 4, Oct 2024)
injuries.detail: Sustained concussion in Week 4 of rookie season, missed 1 game. Cleared through protocol in approximately 10 days. No prior documented concussion history at LSU. While this was an isolated incident with full clearance, any concussion history is worth monitoring given Nabers' contested catch profile. He ranked top-5 in contested targets among all rookies in 2024. Research context: NFL RBs and WRs return to play at a high rate after concussion (89% return same season, missing an average of 1.5 games). Performance metrics generally show no significant acute decline post-concussion. However, Harvard's Football Players Health Study found WRs are 70% more likely to report long-term cognitive impairment compared to lowest-risk positions. Same-season repeat concussion risk is 5.3–8.3% for players who've already had one.
injuries.source: NFL Injury Reports, CBS Sports — Research: Orthopedic Journal of Sports Medicine; Harvard Football Players Health Study

injuries.title: Toe Injury (Late 2024, June 2025)
injuries.detail: Dealt with toe injury in December 2024 (limited practice, listed questionable multiple weeks). Reappeared during June 2025 OTAs, limiting participation. Giants were out of playoff contention in 2024 so the late-season limitations were partly precautionary. Toe injuries in speed WRs can linger and affect burst off the line — worth monitoring but no structural concern reported.

injuries.title: Shoulder / Back (Training Camp 2025)
injuries.detail: Landed on shoulder early in 2025 training camp, sat out practices. Also dealt with a minor back issue that kept him out ~2 weeks in August 2025. Both were precautionary holds and he returned to full practice. No long-term concern.

collins.name: Nico Collins
collins.currentStatus: Healthy entering 2026. Cleared from final concussion (Jan 2026 playoffs) — participated in Pro Bowl flag football game 3 weeks later. Three consecutive 1,000-yard seasons. Primary concern is soft-tissue injury pattern: hamstring issues and multiple concussions have cost him 7 full games and parts of 5 others over the past two seasons.

injuries.title: Concussion #2 — Playoff Wild Card vs. Steelers (Jan 13, 2026)
injuries.detail: Suffered second concussion of the 2025 season during the Texans' wild-card win at Pittsburgh. Fell on his face after catching a slant route, immediately put hands to his face. Carted to locker room, ruled out. Unable to practice all week and was ruled out for the divisional round loss at New England. Cleared ~3 weeks post-injury, participated in Pro Bowl flag football. Research context: The risk of a same-season repeat concussion in the NFL is 5.3–8.3% for players who've already sustained one. Players with multiple concussions within a season typically miss more time from subsequent concussions (median 12 days vs. 8 for first). Long-term, WRs are 70% more likely than low-risk positions to report cognitive impairment later in life (Harvard FPHS). Two concussions in one season is a notable pattern that warrants close monitoring.
injuries.source: ESPN, NY Post, SIC Score — Research: Neurosurgery (2022 — ScienceDirect); Harvard Football Players Health Study

injuries.title: Concussion #1 — Week 7 vs. Seahawks (Oct 21, 2025)
injuries.detail: Head slammed on turf during a catch attempt in the fourth quarter of Monday Night Football at Seattle. Taken to blue tent, then locker room. Ruled out with concussion. Missed Week 8 vs. 49ers. Returned Week 9 vs. Broncos and played the remainder of the regular season without issue. At time of injury, Collins was leading the Texans in receiving yards by a significant margin.
injuries.source: ESPN, SI Texans Daily, SIC Score

injuries.title: Hamstring Strain — Week 5 vs. Bills (Oct 6, 2024)
injuries.detail: Suffered hamstring strain while catching a 67-yard touchdown vs. Buffalo. Initially deemed "day-to-day," later changed to "week-to-week." Placed on IR, missed 4 games (Weeks 6–10). Activated from IR Week 10, returned to action Week 11 vs. Cowboys. Still finished with 68 receptions for 1,006 yards and 7 TDs in just 12 games — his second consecutive 1,000-yard season. Key context: This was a re-aggravation — Collins entered the Bills game already dealing with a hamstring issue. Hamstring injuries in WRs have a recurrence rate of approximately 12–33% within the first year of return, particularly when the initial injury involves re-aggravation. The fact that Collins suffered it on a max-effort play (67-yard TD) suggests the speed demands of his role create ongoing risk for this specific muscle group.
injuries.source: NFL.com, ESPN, PFN, Click2Houston — Research: BJSM hamstring recurrence meta-analyses

injuries.title: Hamstring (2023 Season)
injuries.detail: Dealt with hamstring tightness during the 2023 season. Did not miss significant time. However, the 2024 re-aggravation of the same muscle group suggests a potential pattern. Collins' explosive playing style — 4.44 40-yard dash, 6'4" 222 lbs with deep-threat role — places significant strain on the hamstring complex.

chase.name: Ja'Marr Chase
chase.currentStatus: Healthy entering 2026. Won the receiving triple crown in 2024 (117 rec, 1,708 yds, 17 TD). No significant injuries in 2025. Durable profile — has played 16+ games in 3 of 4 NFL seasons.

injuries.title: Hip Fracture / Labral Tear (Oct 2022)
injuries.detail: Suffered a hairline fracture in his hip during Week 6 vs. the Saints in 2022, which worsened by Week 7. Missed 4 games (Weeks 8–11), returned Week 13 vs. the Chiefs. Still finished with 87 receptions and 1,046 yards despite missing time. The hip is a complex joint for WRs — route-running generates significant rotational force through the hip. Full recovery with no recurrence through 2023-2025 suggests the injury healed well.

injuries.title: Shoulder AC Joint Sprain (Dec 2023)
injuries.detail: Injured shoulder in Week 15 of 2023. Played through it for the final two regular season games and postseason. AC joint sprains are common contact injuries — most resolve in 2-6 weeks without surgery. Did not affect his 2024 production (triple crown season).

nacua.name: Puka Nacua
nacua.currentStatus: Healthy entering 2026. Led NFL in receiving yards per game (95.3) — all-time record. Injury-prone label persists from college (broken foot, ankle issues at BYU) and 2024 PCL injury. Finished 2025 strong despite missing time with ankle and rib injuries.

injuries.title: Low Ankle Sprain — Week 6 vs. Ravens (Oct 2025)
injuries.detail: Sustained left ankle injury during the Rams' victory over Baltimore. Attempted to return in the third quarter but had no targets after re-entry. HC McVay described him as "day-to-day." Missed Week 7 game vs. Jaguars in London. Benefited from Week 8 bye for additional recovery. Returned Week 9 vs. Saints. Ankle sprains are a recurring theme for Nacua — he dealt with multiple ankle issues at BYU and this is at least his second notable ankle injury in the NFL.

injuries.title: PCL Injury — Preseason/Week 1 (2024)
injuries.detail: Suffered a PCL injury during 2024 preseason that was aggravated in Week 1. Missed Weeks 2-7. Despite missing 6 games, still produced 79 catches for 990 yards and 3 TDs. PCL injuries are less common than ACL tears but can affect cutting ability and change-of-direction. The fact that Nacua returned to elite production suggests good structural recovery, but the injury history pattern (college foot fracture, ankle injuries, PCL) is a durability concern.

injuries.title: Rib Injury — Week 9 (Nov 2025)
injuries.detail: Suffered rib injury in third quarter vs. Saints. Could have re-entered but was held out precautionarily with the Rams ahead. Scans showed positive results. Returned Week 10 vs. 49ers without missing a game.

injuries.title: College Injury History (BYU)
injuries.detail: At BYU, Nacua dealt with a broken foot, an ankle injury, and another leg injury that limited his college production and contributed to his fifth-round draft selection. His 2023 rookie year was the first full healthy season of his career. The persistent lower-body injury pattern — foot, ankle, knee (PCL) — suggests structural vulnerability in the lower extremities that warrants ongoing monitoring.

lamb.name: CeeDee Lamb
lamb.currentStatus: Healthy entering 2026. Coming off his worst fantasy season since his rookie year due to a high ankle sprain in 2025. Prior to that, had been one of the most durable WRs in the league with three consecutive 100+ reception seasons.

injuries.title: High Ankle Sprain (2025)
injuries.detail: Suffered a high ankle sprain during the 2025 season that significantly hampered his production. High ankle sprains are more severe than low ankle sprains, typically requiring 6-8 weeks for full recovery. WRs are particularly affected because the injury limits push-off explosiveness, route-running crispness, and the ability to create separation. Lamb's fantasy output dropped notably, marking his worst season since his rookie year. Research shows high ankle sprains in NFL skill players cause an average 4-week absence and residual performance effects for 2-4 weeks after return.
injuries.source: PlayerProfiler Dynasty Rankings, NFL Injury Reports

injuries.title: General Durability (2021-2024)
injuries.detail: Prior to the 2025 ankle sprain, Lamb was one of the most durable WRs in football. Played all 17 games in 2023 (135 rec, 1,749 yds, 12 TD) and 2024 (101 rec, 1,194 yds, 8 TD). Three consecutive seasons with 100+ receptions. His durability profile prior to the ankle injury was elite.

robinson.name: Bijan Robinson
robinson.currentStatus: Healthy entering 2026. First-team All-Pro in 2025. No significant NFL injuries to date. One of the most durable RBs in football — has not missed a game due to injury in his NFL career. College history includes elbow dislocation (2021) and shoulder injury (2022) at Texas.

injuries.title: Shoulder Injury — Week 3, 2024
injuries.detail: Appeared on injury report with shoulder issue in Week 3 of 2024. Did not miss any games. Robinson has shown remarkable durability for a high-volume RB, which is notable given the position's inherent injury risk. Through 3 NFL seasons: 3,910 rushing yards, 1,738 receiving yards, 34 total TDs. His workload (304 carries + 61 targets in 2024 alone) puts him at elevated soft-tissue injury risk going forward.

injuries.title: Elbow Dislocation + Surgery (Nov 2021, Texas)
injuries.detail: Left elbow dislocation during a game at Texas. Required surgery, cleared for return in late February 2022. No recurrence or lingering effects in the NFL. Elbow dislocations are uncommon for RBs but can occur on awkward falls or tackles.

injuries.title: Hamstring/Groin History (High School)
injuries.detail: Dealt with recurring hamstring, groin, knee, and hip strains during high school (2015-2019) at Salpointe Catholic in Tucson. Also had a right fibula fracture in 2013 that required surgery. All resolved before college career. These are worth noting only as baseline history — no recurrence pattern in college or NFL.

achane.name: De'Von Achane
achane.currentStatus: Healthy entering 2026. Achane's elite speed (4.32 40-yard dash, 5'9" 188 lbs) makes him an electrifying playmaker but also raises durability questions. His small frame has led to multiple injuries in his first two seasons. When healthy, he's been one of the most explosive backs in the NFL.

injuries.title: Knee Injury (2024)
injuries.detail: Dealt with a knee injury during the 2024 season that caused him to miss multiple games. Despite availability issues, Achane's per-game production when healthy was elite. His size (5'9" 188 lbs) is both his greatest asset (speed, agility) and his greatest risk factor. Research on undersized NFL RBs shows they tend to have shorter career windows but can be highly productive when healthy. Achane's breakaway speed (top-5 in the NFL in max speed) means he absorbs fewer direct hits than power backs, which partially offsets the size concern.

injuries.title: Knee / Concussion (Rookie, 2023)
injuries.detail: Missed time during his rookie season with knee and concussion injuries. Despite playing only 11 games, averaged 7.8 yards per carry — the highest in the NFL. His injury pattern suggests the biggest risk isn't any single major injury but rather accumulation of smaller ailments that limit availability. Fantasy managers should draft him understanding the weekly volatility.

allen.name: Josh Allen
allen.currentStatus: Healthy entering 2026. Allen's rushing style (700+ yards in multiple seasons) creates elevated injury risk for a franchise QB. Has been remarkably durable despite his physical playing style — has started 16+ games in every season since 2020.

injuries.title: Elbow Injury (2024)
injuries.detail: Dealt with an elbow issue during the 2024 season that was monitored but did not cause him to miss any starts. Allen's throwing mechanics and rushing volume (he's rushed 500+ times in his career) place significant stress on his elbow and shoulder. QB elbow injuries can range from UCL stress to nerve compression. Allen has shown the ability to manage through minor ailments.

injuries.title: General Durability Profile
injuries.detail: Allen has started 100+ regular season games and has not missed significant time due to injury. However, his playing style — he leads all QBs in rushing attempts since 2018 — statistically elevates his injury risk compared to pocket passers. Research shows mobile QBs who rush 100+ times per season have a ~15% higher rate of lower-body injuries. Allen's 6'5" 237 lb frame provides some protection, but the cumulative toll of contact is a long-term monitoring point. Fastest, youngest player to reach 300 total touchdowns in NFL history.

gibbs.name: Jahmyr Gibbs
gibbs.currentStatus: Healthy entering 2026. Gibbs has been one of the most durable young RBs in football — no significant injuries in his first two NFL seasons. His role-share with David Montgomery (prior to Montgomery's departure) may have helped preserve his health by limiting his total touch count.

injuries.title: Hamstring Tightness (2024)
injuries.detail: Appeared on injury reports with hamstring tightness during the 2024 season but did not miss any games. Hamstring issues are common for explosive speed backs — Gibbs ran a 4.36 40-yard dash at the combine. His relatively modest rushing volume (compared to bell-cow backs) has kept him fresh. With Montgomery gone, Gibbs is expected to see a larger workload in 2026, which could change his injury calculus.

injuries.title: College Durability (Alabama/Georgia Tech)
injuries.detail: No significant injuries during his college career at Georgia Tech (2020-2021) or Alabama (2022). Gibbs' 5'9" 200 lb frame and elusive running style mean he avoids big hits more often than power backs, which bodes well for longevity.

jefferson.name: Justin Jefferson
jefferson.currentStatus: Healthy entering 2026. Coming off worst fantasy season as a pro in 2025, partly due to J.J. McCarthy transition at QB. Hamstring concerns linger — missed 7 games in 2023, dealt with hamstring strain again in 2025 training camp. Five consecutive 1,000-yard seasons to open career.

injuries.title: Hamstring Strain — Training Camp (July 2025)
injuries.detail: Left hamstring strain at training camp, missed ~3 weeks of practice and all preseason games. Returned for Week 1. Jefferson himself said he was 'so scared' of re-injury after the 2023 episode. Research: Hamstring recurrence rate for WRs is 12–33% within first year. Same muscle group as 2023 makes this a season-long concern.
injuries.source: Yahoo Sports, Newsweek, Vikings.com, CBS Sports

injuries.title: Hamstring — Missed 7 Games (2023)
injuries.detail: Right hamstring injury in 2023, first significant injury of NFL career. Missed 7 games. Jefferson was visibly emotional about missing time. Despite it, still finished with 68 rec, 1,074 yds, 5 TD in 10 games — per-game ceiling remained elite.

injuries.title: Quad Contusion — Week 2 vs. 49ers (Sept 2024)
injuries.detail: Quad contusion from leg-to-leg contact with Fred Warner. Did not miss any games. Played all 17 in 2024: 103 rec, 1,533 yds, 10 TD.

cmc.name: Christian McCaffrey
cmc.currentStatus: Healthy entering 2026 per Shanahan. Claims 'zero restrictions.' But approaching 30 with bilateral Achilles tendonitis and PCL tear in 2024 — played only 4 games. Calf scare in 2025 preseason raised alarms but played through it. The defining question is durability.

injuries.title: PCL Tear — Week 13 vs. Bills (Dec 2024)
injuries.detail: Attempted to hurdle a defender, landed awkwardly, tearing PCL in right knee. Placed on IR. Only 4 games in 2024: 50 carries, 202 rush yds, 0 TD. PCL tears affect deceleration and cutting. McCaffrey said knee healed 'pretty quickly' by early 2025 offseason.

injuries.title: Bilateral Achilles Tendonitis (2024 Preseason — Week 9)
injuries.detail: Initially listed as 'calf injury,' later clarified as bilateral Achilles tendonitis — both legs. IR for first 8 games. Traveled to Germany for specialist treatment. When he returned Week 10, averaged only 4.0 ypc with max speed 17.4 mph — well below his pre-injury 20+ mph. This is an overuse injury that can recur. SI: 'You never bounce back fully from bilateral Achilles tendonitis.'
injuries.source: ESPN, NBC Sports Bay Area, SI All49ers

injuries.title: Calf Strain — Training Camp (2025)
injuries.detail: Calf issue days into 2025 camp. Alarming because 2024 Achilles was initially listed as 'calf injury.' Shook it off, did not miss regular season. But the calf/Achilles connection will always raise flags.

injuries.title: Hamstring / Ankle (Carolina, 2021)
injuries.detail: Grade 2 hamstring strain Week 3 (missed 5 games). Grade 2 ankle sprain Week 12 (IR, season over). McCaffrey's career defined by 'All-Pro or injured' dichotomy since Panthers days.

stbrown.name: Amon-Ra St. Brown
stbrown.currentStatus: Healthy entering 2026 after offseason knee cleanup surgery. Three consecutive seasons as WR3 or better in fantasy PPG. Dealt with ankle sprain (2025) and knee issue (late 2025) but played through both. One of the most consistent WRs in football.

injuries.title: Knee Surgery — Offseason (Feb 2025)
injuries.detail: Underwent knee surgery shortly after 2024 season ended. Described it as a cleanup to address lingering issues. Missed OTAs while rehabbing but said he would be ready for training camp. Played all 17 games in 2024 (115 rec, 1,263 yds, career-high 12 TD) despite the underlying issue. The knee was clearly something he managed all season.

injuries.title: Ankle Sprain — Week 13 (Dec 2025)
injuries.detail: Ankle sprain sustained during 2025 season. Listed as non-participant in practice before Cowboys game. Lions teammates and coaches described him as someone who 'always plays' — and he did. Also dealt with a knee issue in Weeks 16-17 but suited up for both games. St. Brown's durability despite nagging injuries is a defining trait.
injuries.source: Athlon Sports, Heavy, Pride of Detroit

burrow.name: Joe Burrow
burrow.currentStatus: Recovering from Grade 3 turf toe surgery (Sept 2025). Has missed significant time in 3 of 6 NFL seasons. When healthy, elite — led NFL with 4,918 yds and 43 TD in 2024, winning 2nd Comeback Player of the Year. The question is always durability.

injuries.title: Grade 3 Turf Toe — Week 2 vs. Jaguars (Sept 2025)
injuries.detail: Sustained turf toe when sacked in second quarter. Right foot trapped under defender. Required surgery, estimated minimum 3-month recovery. Put potential return in mid-December 2025. This is Burrow's third season-ending or near-season-ending injury in 6 NFL years. Grade 3 turf toe involves a complete tear of the plantar plate — significantly impacts push-off and mobility for QBs.

injuries.title: Wrist Ligament Tear — Week 11 vs. Ravens (Nov 2023)
injuries.detail: Felt a 'pop' in his throwing hand while delivering a TD pass. Torn ligament in right wrist required season-ending surgery. Missed final 7 games. Returned in 2024 and admitted the wrist was 'still not 100%' but threw for 4,918 yds and 43 TD anyway — winning Comeback Player of the Year for the second time.

injuries.title: ACL/MCL/PCL/Meniscus Tear — Week 11 (Nov 2020)
injuries.detail: As a rookie, suffered devastating multi-ligament knee tear vs. Washington: torn ACL, MCL, PCL, and meniscus in left knee. Season-ending. Returned the following year and led the Bengals to the Super Bowl. This recovery remains one of the most impressive in recent NFL history, but the cumulative damage to Burrow's body is a long-term concern.

injuries.title: Appendectomy — Training Camp (Aug 2022)
injuries.detail: Ruptured appendix requiring emergency surgery during training camp. Recovered in time for Week 1. Unusual for football injury profiles but worth noting as part of Burrow's extensive medical history.

injuries.title: Calf Strain — Training Camp (July 2023)
injuries.detail: Right calf strain at training camp. Did not miss regular season time. The calf issue preceded his wrist tear later that year.

jsn.name: Jaxon Smith-Njigba
jsn.currentStatus: Healthy entering 2026. Led NFL in receiving yards in 2025. Broke out in sophomore season after injury-limited time at Ohio State. Durability has been clean since entering the NFL — the college hamstring history appears fully behind him.

injuries.title: Hamstring — Ohio State (2022 Season)
injuries.detail: Suffered a hamstring injury early in his final season at Ohio State that limited him to just 5 games. This significantly impacted his draft stock — fell to pick #20 despite being considered a top-5 talent. The hamstring issue was a major concern for NFL teams. However, JSN has shown zero recurrence in two full NFL seasons, suggesting the injury was a one-time setback. His 2025 season (NFL receiving yards leader) put those concerns fully to rest.
injuries.source: NFL Draft profiles, Ohio State records

bowers.name: Brock Bowers
bowers.currentStatus: Healthy entering 2026. Set the all-time NFL rookie record for receiving yards by a TE in 2024. Durability was the one concern at Georgia — ankle injury in 2023 required surgery. Has been healthy throughout NFL career so far.

injuries.title: Ankle Surgery (2023, Georgia)
injuries.detail: Suffered an ankle injury during his final season at Georgia that required surgery. Missed time but returned for the College Football Playoff. The surgical repair appears fully healed — Bowers had no ankle issues during his record-breaking rookie season. TEs with ankle surgery history should be monitored long-term due to the position's blocking demands.

hurts.name: Jalen Hurts
hurts.currentStatus: Healthy entering 2026. Concussion history is the primary concern — has suffered multiple concussions in his NFL career, including a significant one in 2024 that forced him to miss games during a playoff push.

injuries.title: Concussion — Late 2024 Season
injuries.detail: Suffered a concussion during the 2024 season that caused him to miss games during a critical stretch. Hurts' rushing style (700+ yards multiple seasons) exposes him to more head contact than pocket passers. Research: QBs who rush frequently have elevated concussion risk. Multiple concussions raise long-term cognitive concerns and increase same-season repeat risk (5.3–8.3%).

injuries.title: Knee / Shoulder Injuries (2022-2023)
injuries.detail: Dealt with shoulder and knee issues at various points that limited his mobility but rarely caused him to miss starts. Hurts has shown remarkable toughness playing through injuries. However, his dual-threat style means the cumulative toll is higher than for traditional pocket QBs.

henry.name: Derrick Henry
henry.currentStatus: Healthy entering 2026. Defying father time — rushed for 1,921 yards in 2024 (age 30), then remained productive in 2025. Jones fracture (2021) is the only significant injury in his career. His workload (2,000+ career carries) is historically unprecedented for a healthy RB at this age.

injuries.title: Jones Fracture — Right Foot (Oct 2021)
injuries.detail: Suffered a Jones fracture (5th metatarsal) in his right foot during the 2021 season. Missed 9 games. Returned for the playoffs and rushed for 195 yards in the wild-card round. Jones fractures in NFL players have a ~85% return-to-play rate but carry a 15-25% refracture risk. Henry has had zero recurrence in 4+ years, suggesting complete healing. For a power back with his workload, this durability profile is historically elite.

mcbride.name: Trey McBride
mcbride.currentStatus: Healthy entering 2026. Consensus TE1 in fantasy for 2026. Has been remarkably durable — no significant injuries in his NFL career. Breakout 2024 season (111 rec, 1,146 yds) established him as an elite TE.

injuries.title: General Durability
injuries.detail: No significant injuries in 3 NFL seasons. McBride's durability is one of his most valuable traits for fantasy — TE is a position plagued by injuries (Kelce, Kittle, Pitts, Andrews have all missed significant time). McBride's clean medical profile is a competitive advantage.

kelce.name: Travis Kelce
kelce.currentStatus: Healthy entering 2026 at age 36. Cut 25 lbs in offseason to extend career. Has had 10 surgeries throughout career. Bone bruise (2023), ankle sprain (2023), knee hyperextension (2023 camp) are recent concerns. Still produced 50 rec, 631 yds, 4 TD through 10 games in 2025.

injuries.title: Bone Bruise — Knee (Sept 2023)
injuries.detail: Hyperextended knee at practice before 2023 season opener. Bone bruise diagnosed. Missed Week 1 vs. Lions — first game missed due to injury since 2013 (his rookie year). Returned Week 2 and played through the season, though he looked slower early on. Came alive in the playoffs.
injuries.source: NFL.com, SI Chiefs, Fox News, Sportskeeda

injuries.title: Low Ankle Sprain (Oct 2023)
injuries.detail: Sustained ankle sprain Week 5 of 2023 season. Played through it for the remainder of the year but production dipped mid-season — Kelce jokingly blamed it on being "f—— old." Did not miss a game. Came alive in the playoffs with vintage performances.

injuries.title: Knee Surgery — Cartilage (Rookie, 2013)
injuries.detail: Injured knee in preseason of his rookie year. Arthroscopic surgery revealed a cartilage issue. Missed all but 1 game in 2013. Has been remarkably durable since — missed only 1 game in the next 11 seasons due to injury.

injuries.title: 10 Career Surgeries — Cumulative Toll
injuries.detail: Kelce has revealed he has had 10 surgeries throughout his career, saying "More than anyone could ever imagine" about the pain. At 36, the cumulative toll is the primary concern. He cut 25 lbs in the 2025 offseason to reduce joint stress. His durability (missed only 2 games in 12 seasons) is historically elite for a TE, but age and the surgical history mean the cliff could come at any time.

kittle.name: George Kittle
kittle.currentStatus: Recovering from torn right Achilles suffered in the 2026 NFL Playoffs vs. Eagles (Jan 2026). Expected 9-12 month recovery. Has extensive injury history — foot fracture (2020), groin (2020), multiple hamstring issues (2024-2025), ankle sprain (2025). When healthy, one of the best TEs in NFL history.

injuries.title: Torn Achilles — Playoffs vs. Eagles (Jan 2026)
injuries.detail: Tore right Achilles catching a 6-yard pass from Brock Purdy in the wild-card win over Philadelphia. Ruled out for rest of playoffs. Expected 9-12 month recovery timeline. Research: TE Achilles tears have better return rates than WRs (~55% vs 38% for WRs) but still carry significant performance decline. At age 32, this injury creates serious questions about Kittle's future.

injuries.title: Grade 3 Hamstring Tear — Week 1 (Sept 2025)
injuries.detail: Suffered Grade 3 (complete) hamstring tear in Week 1 vs. Seahawks after catching 4 passes for 25 yds and a TD. Placed on IR, missed 5 games. Returned Oct 15. Grade 3 tears are the most severe — complete rupture of muscle fibers. This was a pattern continuation from 2024 hamstring issues.

injuries.title: Ankle Sprain — Week 16 (Dec 2025)
injuries.detail: Left ankle sprain vs. Colts. Had 7 rec, 115 yds, 1 TD before leaving. Missed 1 game, returned. This was sandwiched between the hamstring and eventual Achilles tear — a brutal 2025 injury sequence.

injuries.title: Hamstring Sprain — Week 11 (Nov 2024)
injuries.detail: One-game absence due to hamstring sprain. This was a precursor to the more severe 2025 hamstring tear. Pattern of hamstring issues developing in his early 30s.

injuries.title: Foot Fracture — IR (2020)
injuries.detail: Fractured foot in 2020, placed on IR. Missed 8 games. This was the first major injury of Kittle's career and signaled the beginning of a pattern of soft-tissue issues.

london.name: Drake London
london.currentStatus: Healthy entering 2026. Broke out in 2024 with 100 rec, 1,271 yds, 9 TD. Shoulder issue in 2025 Week 1 was monitored but he played through it. College ankle fracture (2021) is the only major injury in his history.

injuries.title: Shoulder Injury — Week 1 (Sept 2025)
injuries.detail: Held out of Atlanta's final drive in Week 1 with a shoulder injury. Monitored closely in Week 2 but continued to play. Did not miss any games. London's physical playing style (6'4" 219 lbs, contested catch specialist) means shoulder issues are an ongoing risk.

injuries.title: Ankle Fracture — College (Oct 2021, USC)
injuries.detail: Fractured right ankle during USC's 8th game of the 2021 season. Missed remainder of the year. Despite this, was still drafted 8th overall by the Falcons. Full recovery — no ankle issues in 3 NFL seasons. Named Pac-12 Offensive Player of the Year before the injury.

taylor.name: Jonathan Taylor
taylor.currentStatus: Healthy entering 2026. Bounce-back seasons in 2024-2025 after the ankle injury that derailed his 2022-2023. Still only 27 — in his prime if healthy.

injuries.title: Ankle Injury — IR (2022-2023)
injuries.detail: High ankle sprain in 2022 that lingered into 2023. Combined with a contract holdout in 2023, Taylor missed significant time over two seasons. When he returned healthy in 2024, he showed he still had elite talent. High ankle sprains in RBs are particularly impactful because they affect cutting and acceleration.

daniels.name: Jayden Daniels
daniels.currentStatus: Healthy entering 2026. Offensive Rookie of the Year in 2024. Dual-threat style (891 rush yds as rookie) creates elevated injury risk similar to Lamar Jackson and Jalen Hurts. Rib injury in 2024 playoffs was his only notable NFL injury.

injuries.title: Rib Injury — 2024 Playoffs
injuries.detail: Sustained rib injury during the Commanders' 2024 playoff run. Played through it but was visibly limited. Rib injuries in QBs affect throwing mechanics and willingness to take hits. Daniels' rushing volume (150+ carries as a rookie) means he takes more contact than pocket passers, elevating all injury risks.

laporta.name: Sam LaPorta
laporta.currentStatus: Recovering from back surgery. Had back issues throughout 2025 that limited his production compared to his breakout rookie season. The surgery is a concern for a young TE — back injuries can be career-altering.

injuries.title: Back Surgery — Offseason (Jan/Feb 2026)
injuries.detail: Underwent back surgery after the 2025 season. The first time he offered insight into the injury publicly. Back injuries in TEs are particularly concerning because the position demands both blocking (spinal compression) and route-running (rotational stress). LaPorta's breakout rookie year (86 rec, 889 yds, 10 TD) made him a top-3 dynasty TE, but back surgery at age 24 introduces real long-term risk.
injuries.source: Pride of Detroit, Dan Campbell press conferences

rice.name: Rashee Rice
rice.currentStatus: Serving 30-day jail sentence for probation violation (May 2026). Was suspended 6 games to start 2025 season for personal conduct policy violation. Returned from 2024 LCL tear and participated fully in camp/preseason before suspension. Currently missing OTAs. Contract year — future with Chiefs uncertain.

injuries.title: LCL Tear + Lateral Hamstring Tendon Repair — Week 4 (Sept 2024)
injuries.detail: Tore the lateral collateral ligament (LCL) in his knee during Week 4. Also required lateral hamstring tendon repair. Fortunately, no ACL or other internal knee joint damage. LCL tears are less common than MCL tears but can be equally debilitating. Andy Reid confirmed Rice was a full participant at 2025 OTAs and minicamp. Patrick Mahomes praised his recovery progress. Research: LCL reconstruction has ~85% return-to-sport rate, but combined with hamstring tendon repair adds complexity.
injuries.source: ESPN (Stephania Bell), NFL.com, SI, Arrowhead Pride

injuries.title: 6-Game Suspension — Personal Conduct (Aug 2025)
injuries.detail: Suspended without pay for first 6 games of 2025 for violating NFL personal conduct policy stemming from March 2024 multi-vehicle collision in Dallas. Rice pleaded guilty to two third-degree felony charges. Later violated probation, sentenced to 30 days in jail (serving May 2026). The off-field issues compound the injury concerns — Chiefs may not extend him.

olave.name: Chris Olave
olave.currentStatus: Returning from concussion that ended his 2024 season. Has had multiple concussions in his NFL career — the pattern is the primary concern. When healthy, elite route-runner with back-to-back 1,000-yard seasons to start career.

injuries.title: Concussion — Season-Ending (Nov 2024)
injuries.detail: Suffered a concussion in November 2024 that ended his season. This was not his first NFL concussion — the recurring pattern is the most alarming aspect of Olave's medical profile. ESPN's Stephania Bell flagged Olave's concussion history as a top concern heading into 2025. Research: Players with 3+ career concussions have significantly elevated risk for each subsequent concussion, longer recovery times, and increased long-term cognitive concerns. WRs who run contested routes (Olave's specialty) are particularly exposed.

injuries.title: Prior Concussion History
injuries.detail: Olave has suffered multiple concussions during his NFL career. The exact count is not fully public, but the pattern is well-documented enough that ESPN's injury analyst specifically flagged it as a 2025 fantasy concern. Each successive concussion typically results in longer recovery time and lower threshold for the next one. This is a dynasty-altering concern for a player who is otherwise an elite talent.

pickens.name: George Pickens
pickens.currentStatus: Healthy entering 2026 with new team (traded to Cowboys). ACL tear at Georgia (2021) is the major injury in his history. Has been relatively healthy in the NFL but behavioral concerns have followed him — traded from Pittsburgh partly due to character issues.

injuries.title: ACL Tear — Spring Practice (Mar 2021, Georgia)
injuries.detail: Tore ACL during spring practice at Georgia in March 2021. Remarkably, returned by Week 4 of the 2021 season and played in 8 games, contributing to Georgia's national championship run. The aggressive return timeline raised eyebrows but Pickens showed no ill effects. Has not had any ACL-related issues in 3 NFL seasons. Research: ACL re-injury risk is ~25% within 2-3 years, but Pickens is now 4+ years post-surgery with no recurrence, which significantly lowers ongoing risk.

injuries.title: Hamstring Tightness (2024)
injuries.detail: Dealt with minor hamstring tightness during 2024 season with Pittsburgh. Did not miss games. Worth noting only because hamstring issues can become recurring for explosive WRs.

cook.name: James Cook III
cook.currentStatus: Healthy entering 2026. One of the most durable RBs in the league — has not missed significant time in 3 NFL seasons. Emerged as a bell-cow back in 2024 with 271 carries for 1,009 yards.

injuries.title: Toe Injury (2024)
injuries.detail: Dealt with a toe issue during the 2024 season. Appeared on injury reports but did not miss games. Toe injuries in RBs can linger and affect burst, but Cook showed no production decline. Finished with career highs in carries (271), rushing yards (1,009), and TDs (16).

injuries.title: General Durability
injuries.detail: Cook has one of the cleanest injury profiles among starting RBs. Has played in all 17 regular season games in multiple seasons. His running style — patient and decisive rather than power-based — may contribute to his durability. At 5'11" 210 lbs, he's not undersized like Achane but not a bruiser either.

jlove.name: Jeremiyah Love
jlove.currentStatus: Healthy entering 2026 rookie season. 2025 first-round pick from Notre Dame. No significant injury history in college. Elite speed (4.36 40-yard dash) and explosiveness. Primary concern is typical rookie workload adjustment.

injuries.title: College Durability (Notre Dame)
injuries.detail: No significant injuries during his college career at Notre Dame. Love was a key contributor to Notre Dame's College Football Playoff run in 2024. His speed (4.36 40) and elusiveness mean he avoids big hits, similar to players like Jahmyr Gibbs. Clean medical history is a positive indicator for NFL durability.

jeanty.name: Ashton Jeanty
jeanty.currentStatus: Healthy entering 2026 rookie season. 2025 second overall pick from Boise State. Heisman runner-up with historic 2,601-yard rushing season in 2024. Minor ankle sprain in college but otherwise clean profile.

injuries.title: Ankle Sprain (2024, Boise State)
injuries.detail: Dealt with a minor ankle sprain during his historic 2024 season at Boise State. Did not miss games. Jeanty still rushed for 2,601 yards and 29 TDs — the second-most rushing yards in FBS history. The ankle clearly did not limit his production. At 5'9" 215 lbs, Jeanty has a more compact, powerful build than typical speed backs, which may help with NFL durability.

injuries.title: Workload Concern — 344 Carries (2024)
injuries.detail: Jeanty carried the ball 344 times in 2024 alone — an extremely high volume for a college back. Research shows that college RBs with 300+ carry seasons have slightly elevated injury risk in their first NFL year due to cumulative wear. However, Jeanty was 20 years old during that season and showed no signs of breakdown.

jackson.name: Lamar Jackson
jackson.currentStatus: Healthy entering 2026. Two-time MVP. Rushing style (900+ rush yards in multiple seasons) creates elevated injury risk but Jackson has been remarkably durable since the 2021 ankle sprain. Missed only 2 games due to injury from 2022-2025.

injuries.title: Knee Injury — Week 13, 2022 / Playoff Miss (Jan 2023)
injuries.detail: Suffered a PCL strain in Week 13 of the 2022 season. Missed the final 5 regular season games and the Ravens' wild-card playoff loss to the Bengals. Jackson's absence in the playoffs was a defining moment — the Ravens were the #1 seed and lost at home. The PCL strain healed without surgery. Research: PCL injuries in QBs who rush frequently carry elevated re-injury risk due to deceleration demands.
injuries.source: ESPN, NFL Injury Reports, Ravens official

injuries.title: Ankle Sprain — Week 14, 2021
injuries.detail: Bone bruise / ankle sprain suffered in Week 14 vs. Cleveland. Missed final 4 regular season games. The Ravens collapsed without Jackson, going 1-3 and missing the playoffs. This was the first significant injury of Jackson's career and raised questions about the long-term viability of his rushing-dependent style. He has since proven those concerns mostly unfounded with 3 healthy seasons.

injuries.title: Rushing QB Durability Profile
injuries.detail: Jackson has rushed 1,000+ times in his career — more than any QB in NFL history through their first 7 seasons. Research on mobile QBs shows those who rush 100+ times per season have approximately 15% higher rate of lower-body injuries than pocket passers. Jackson's 6'2" 212 lb frame is lighter than Josh Allen (237 lbs) which provides less protection on contact. However, his elusiveness and willingness to slide/go out of bounds has improved significantly since 2021, reducing his hit exposure.
